title: Indian Defence Estates Service officer trainees call on Raksha Mantri
body_text:
The Officer Trainees of the Indian Defence Estates Service (2025 Batch), undergoing training at the National Institute of Defence Estates Management (NIDEM), called on Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh in New Delhi on August 17, 2026. Raksha Mantri appreciated the role of the Defence Estates Department in the management of defence land and municipal administration of the Cantonment Boards across the country.
Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised the role of public servants in meeting the evolving aspirations of the citizens. He said civil servants must play a major role with utmost ‘Seva Bhav’, delivering the services in a people-friendly manner. He added that the officers should meet people regularly and listen to their grievances to understand their concerns and instill a sense of assurance.
Raksha Mantri emphasised that public servants and budding officers should pay equal attention to their physical and mental well-being, urging them to follow a spiritual path and practise meditation. Director General Defence Estates Smt Shobha Gupta was present during the interaction

enrichment.summary: Officer Trainees of the Indian Defence Estates Service (2025 Batch), training at the National Institute of Defence Estates Management (NIDEM), met Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh in New Delhi on August 17, 2026. He praised the Defence Estates Department's role in managing defence land and Cantonment Board administration, and urged the trainees to serve with 'Seva Bhav', engage regularly with citizens, and maintain physical and mental well-being through spirituality and meditation.
enrichment.context: This is a courtesy call/interaction event, a routine part of induction training for civil service officer trainees, where a minister offers general advice on public service values. The Indian Defence Estates Service (IDES) is a Group A central civil service under the Ministry of Defence responsible for managing defence lands and the civic administration of Cantonment Boards across India, trained at NIDEM in Delhi. Such interactions have no policy or administrative content beyond motivational remarks and do not signal any change in scheme, law, or institutional structure.
